title: Elkhorn Ranch house (T.R.'s 'home ranch'), built Oct 1884 - spring 1885 by W.W. Sewall and W. Dow; recommended state = summer 1886 (date of T.R.'s photographs)
units: feet (ft), feet-inches (ft_in) and metres (m) given for every dimension

coordinate_system.origin: south-west outside corner of the log wall faces (log ends project beyond this), Z=0 at finished grade beside the house (terrace varies <1 ft over the site per Taylor 1959 p.18)
coordinate_system.X: +east, perpendicular to the long walls (0 = west face, 30 = east face)
coordinate_system.Y: +north, along the long axis (0 = south face, 60 = north face)
coordinate_system.orientation_note: Long axis is 'site north'. On the 1957/59 excavation map the house axis sits ~10.7 deg clockwise of Beaubien's baseline, which itself is ~N16W +/-5 -> house long axis ~N5W +/-6 deg true. Use your solved layout for placement.
coordinate_system.elevation_naming: east elevation faces the river (front); south gable end has the piazza; west = back (kitchen door, cellar hatch)

sources.TAY59: Taylor, D.C. 1959, Archeological Investigations of the Elkhorn Ranch Site (TRC thro_639-758; OCR layout/text/taylor1959_ocr)
sources.MAP57: Beaubien 1957 / Taylor 1959 excavation map, 1 in = 30 ft (mosaic layout/img/taylor/beaubien_taylor_map_mosaic_approx.png, 5.0 px/ft); positions converted to house coords by bilinear fit to the excavated 60x30 house outline (scripts in spec/derivations)
sources.MAT60: Mattison, R.H. 1960, Elkhorn Ranch buildings report (MWAC 6_41; layout/text/mattison1960_ocr)
sources.SEW19: Sewall, W.W. 1919, Bill Sewall's Story of T.R., pp.18-19 ('sixty feet long, thirty feet wide, and seven feet high, with a flat roof and a porch')
sources.SEWLTR: W.W. Sewall letters (Cunningham Coll.) quoted by Mattison 1960: Oct 19 1884 ('very flat roof', 9 ft high), Feb 18 1885 ('have got it shingled and the under floor layed'), Dec 20 1885 (stables 16x20, 12 ft space, logs hewn on three sides)
sources.TRSK: T.R.'s pencil sketch plan + end elevation + lumber list (Cunningham Coll.; Mattison 1960 photo 7 = MWAC_6_41_24; NPS redraw by D.E. Rogers 1-27-59 = MWAC_6_41_2/3)
sources.EDITH: Edith K. Roosevelt letter-sketch plan from the Elkhorn, 1890 (Mattison 1960 photo 6 = MWAC_6_41_26)
sources.BP: Harvard-collection blueprint 'Elkhorn Ranch, Little Missouri River, Dakota', plan + E and S elevations at 1/4in=1ft (HSR App. B, layout/img/hsr_appB-78.png). Measured: 24.63 px/ft horizontally, 25.47 px/ft vertically on the scan. A 20th-c. reconstruction drawing, NOT a survey: used only where it agrees with photos/excavation
sources.P_PIAZZA: T.R. photo 1886, east veranda with antlers (best scan: model/ref/trc_thrb/THRB03304-00217.jpg; also MWAC_1255_5_12a/12c, Sewall 1919 p.132, Hagedorn 1921 p.454)
sources.P_HOUSE: T.R. photo 1886, house among cottonwoods from SE (best scan: model/ref/trc_thrb/THRB03297-00402.jpg; also MWAC_1255_5_14c, Sewall p.46, Taylor fig.19)
sources.P_RIVER: T.R. photo 1886 from east bank across the Little Missouri (best scan: model/ref/trc_mwac1950/MWAC_1255_5_13b.jpg; also Harvard print via model/ref/harvard_via_astheyare/tr-6.jpg, Sewall p.46, Hagedorn p.318, Taylor fig.2)
sources.P_STABLE: T.R. photo 1886, stables close-up from S (best scan: model/ref/trc_thrb/THRB03296-00401.jpg; also MWAC_1255_5_7a/7b, Hagedorn p.514, Taylor fig.21)
sources.P_CORRALS: T.R. photo 1886, barn + utility shed + corrals looking N from 25 ft W of well (model/ref/trc_mwac1950/MWAC_1255_5_9a.jpg, 8a; Taylor fig.22)
sources.TRBOOK: T.R., Hunting Trips of a Ranchman (1885) pp.15-16, Ranch Life and the Hunting-Trail (1888) pp.25-27
sources.GIFFORD: R. Swain Gifford engraving 'Elkhorn Ranch-house', Hunting Trips 1885 - artist's rendering, low weight (shows full-length veranda; contradicted by photos/excavation)

length_N_S.source: SEW19 '60 ft long'; MAP57 excavated outline 59.5 ft; BP 60'-0"

width_E_W.source: SEW19 '30 ft wide'; MAP57 30.6 ft; BP 30'-0"; TRSK end elevation 12+4+14=30

footprint.note: Dimensions are to the outside faces of the hewn logs. Corner log ends project a further ~12 in (see corners).

foundation.type: hewn cottonwood sill logs laid on isolated fine-grained sandstone boulders (no continuous footing); cellar under SW quarter
foundation.stones_found: Taylor 1959 p.33-34: nine partially visible sandstone boulders, buff/orange/deep red, plus small shims; SW corner stone missing (reported moved to State Capitol grounds, Bismarck). Exposed thicknesses listed by Taylor range 3.5in - ~16in.

stone_positions_from_MAP57.where: west wall, N of cellar hatch ('big block north of cellar entry')
east wall, 'long stone south of [NE] corner'
south wall, W of hall door

foundation.stone_size_model: irregular slabs ~2'0" x 1'6" in plan, 6-16 in thick, top at Z 0'3"-0'6", set under the sill so ~3-6 in shows; sizes are estimates from the 1:360 map symbols
foundation.map_uncertainty: +/-1.5 ft (mosaic seam +/-4 ft is far from the house; symbol size ~1-2 ft)

log_walls.species: cottonwood, cut near the site (TAY59 p.33; MAT60 p.4)

face_height.source: P_PIAZZA: 7 log courses between the dark sill band and the plate over a 9 ft wall; TAY59 'each timber well over a foot square'

thickness.source: estimate: hewn faces in/out; end grain in P_PIAZZA shows ~12x10 in blocks with waney rounded corners

section.hewing: hewn flat on outside and inside faces and on the bed (Sewall: 'we hew the logs on three sides' for the stables, same crew/method); broad-axe score marks and checks clearly visible in P_PIAZZA; corners waney/rounded; top of each log left slightly rounded where it beds into the joint
section.chinking: tight hewn beds: joint visible as a dark line 1/2 - 1 in; no light-coloured daubing visible in P_PIAZZA; model 3/4 in recessed dark (mud/clay) chink, recessed 1 in

course_stack.derivation: P_PIAZZA (THRB03304-00217), SE corner strip at 148 px/ft (scale from window lights ~13in per light+muntin): eave at y=60, dark band 1140-1250, sill log 1250-1400, grade ~1400 -> eave 9.05 ft above grade; 7 log courses + sill. Confirmed by P_RIVER (eave 8.6 +/-1 ft) and BP east elevation (9.2 ft). Sewall 1919 '7 ft high' = interior clear height (T.R.'s sketch end elevation shows a 7 1/2 ft wall); Sewall letter 1884 '9 ft high' = exterior. Both reconciled by this stack.
course_stack.dark_band_note: P_PIAZZA shows a continuous dark band ~8 in high at Z ~1'4"-2'0" along the east wall south of the veranda (between sill and course 2). Interpretation uncertain (deep unchinked joint, sill face set back, or darker/charred log). Recommend modelling course 2 recessed 2-3 in with a darker material.

plate_top_z.source: course stack (8 x 13.25 in from Z 0'6")

corners.type: notched and lapped corners with projecting ends (crowns), alternate courses projecting in each direction
corners.evidence: P_PIAZZA SE corner: squared log ends with visible end grain project beyond both wall faces; a notch cut is visible on the upper face of several projecting ends; BP elevations draw the same staggered square ends.
corners.notch_recommendation: saddle-type notch cut on the underside of each hewn log over the log below (Maine woodsman practice), crown left square; NOT dovetail (no flush corners), NOT post-and-sill (no corner posts visible). Exact notch geometry not resolvable in the 1600-px scans.

projection.source: P_PIAZZA: projecting blocks ~150 px at 148 px/ft

corners.end_finish: ends sawn/axed square, irregular lengths (+/-3 in)

log_walls.interior_face: hewn log faces, probably whitewashed (unknown); rooms divided by board partitions

finished_floor_z.source: top of sill log; door thresholds sit on the sill (P_PIAZZA door head aligns with window heads)

floor.construction: double pine floor (BP note 'Double pine floor'; Sewall Feb 1885 'under floor layed'; lumber list 6,000 bf floor boards, 15 ft) on 2x6 floor joists (lumber list '2x6, 500 ft') and irregular cottonwood floor beams (BP note) spanning E-W from sill to sill with mid-bearing on the hall partitions
floor.board: pine, planed one side, 1 in x 6-8 in, two layers

roof.type: gable, wood-shingled, ridge running N-S (along the 60 ft axis), gables at south and north ends

derivation: T.R. sketch end elevation (MWAC_6_41_24/Rogers redraw): 30 ft span, rafters marked 18 ft, drawn apex 9.2 ft above wall -> 31.5 deg
BP south elevation: rise 138 px over half-span 237 px -> 30.2 deg

P_RIVER (MWAC_1255_5_13b, near-elevation from ~E, ~600 ft): projected rise eave->ridge 42 px on house scale 4.5 px/ft -> 9.3 ft over 16 ft (15 ft + 1 ft overhang) -> 30.2 deg; camera height error +/-1.5 deg
lumber list: 2x6 rafters 20 ft long (cut to 18 ft) -> 30 deg needs 17.3 ft + overhang = 18 ft (consistent)
pitch_deg.conflict: Sewall letter Oct 1884 'the house is to have a very flat roof' and Sewall 1919 'flat roof' describe the plan/recollection; all three photographs show a clear gable of ~30 deg. Photos win.

ridge_z.source: plate top + 15 ft x tan30 (to top of rafter at ridge line); shingle surface adds ~0.15 ft

spacing.source: lumber list 1,000 bf of 2x6x20 = 50 rafters = 25 pairs over 60 ft -> 2'6" o.c.

rafters.ridge: rafters butted at ridge, no ridge beam visible (assumption)

roof.ceiling_joists: 2x4 x 16 ft (lumber list '2x4, 16 ft, 500 bf') spanning from plate to the hall partitions, ~2'0" o.c.; 'single floor overhead' (Sewall) = boarded ceiling

eave_overhang_horizontal.source: P_PIAZZA corner shows short eave beyond log face; rafter-length check (18 ft rafter at 30 deg)

roof.eave_fascia: 1x6 board fascia on rafter tails; open soffit (rafter tails visible) - photo shows thin eave edge

rake_overhang.source: P_HOUSE shows a light rake board standing proud of the shingled gable

roof.rake_board: 1x6 pine barge board along both rakes, plain
roof.sheathing: 1 in pine roof boards, 16 ft (lumber list 3,600 bf), laid tight

shingles.material: sawn pine shingles (Sewall Feb 1885 'Have got it shingled'; 'All boards and shingles here is pine')

exposure.source: period standard for 16 in shingles on a 7:12 roof; not measurable in the scans

shingles.courses_per_slope: approx 42 (17.3 ft slope + 1.15 ft overhang / 5 in)

gables.construction: framed gable (2x4 studs on the plate log) sheathed and covered with sawn shingles, 5 in exposure; MAT60: 'the photographs indicate that the south gable and the piazza were shingled' - confirmed in P_HOUSE (fine shingle texture on the S gable)

south_gable_window.lights: 6 lights (2 wide x 3 high) single sash - P_HOUSE shows 2 lights wide; BP draws 4

north_gable_window.note: no photograph of the north end; TAY59 'I would guess that it was [present]'. Recommend mirror of south gable window (conjectural).

doors_common.leaf: 2'8" x 6'6" (BP note 'Doors about 2'8" x 7'0", some of matched pine boards'; 6'6" fits the log-course head in P_PIAZZA)

head_z.source: top of course 7; P_PIAZZA door head aligns with window heads within ~4 in

doors_common.construction: vertical matched pine boards on 3 battens (ledged), strap hinges; plain board casing 3.5 in

east_elevation_X30.evidence: TAY59: 'six windows and a door. Two windows were south of the door, four north of it.' P_PIAZZA confirms the sequence W1 (outside veranda), W2 (under veranda), DOOR, W3...W6. Positions measured on BP plan (24.63 px/ft); a 1-D projective fit of these positions to their image x in P_PIAZZA leaves residuals <=1.5 ft, and the fit places the veranda's south end at Y=9.2-9.5 ft, matching the excavation (9.2).

rough_opening_h.source: derived: P_PIAZZA window frame spans ~4.5 log courses (between top of course 2 and top of course 6); 2 rows of ~10in lights per sash

east_veranda.evidence: TAY59 p.48 'a low, roofed porch, an area 6 feet wide by 22 feet long ... beams which supported the veranda's roof extended out from the edge of the cabin and rested on a pair of vertical posts'; MAP57 outline converts to X 30-36.3, Y 9.2-31.7; EDITH 1890 sketch puts it opposite the middle east room, ~10.7-31.6 ft from the S end; projective fit of P_PIAZZA gives south end at Y 9.2-9.5.

depth_X.source: MAP57 6.3 ft (bilinear conversion) and TAY59 text '6 feet wide'
depth_X.note: CONFLICT: BP draws 9.7 ft, Rogers redraw of T.R.'s plan 10 ft x 40 ft (the plan, not as built), and a weak camera solve of P_PIAZZA suggests ~9-11 ft. Excavated outline + Taylor text win; validate with camera match #1 (if the SE post lands well left of the right frame edge when everything else lines up, deepen toward 8 ft).

deck_z_top.source: P_PIAZZA: floor edge log + plank ~one log above ground; step ~7 in down from threshold

east_veranda.deck: pine planks (1.5-2 in) running N-S on log sleepers; a round log ~8 in dia forms the visible front edge (P_PIAZZA); timbers recovered in 1959 (TAY59 p.34)

section.source: P_PIAZZA: squared/hewn post at right edge, ~1/25 of veranda length in perspective

posts.on: flat stones (TAY59 'stones under the front veranda')
posts.note: 22 ft clear span on a single hewn beam - if this reads wrong in renders, add a mid post (no evidence).

roof.form: nearly flat shed roof springing from the main eave line

z_at_wall.source: ledger at plate (beams 'extended out from the edge of the cabin')

z_front_beam_top.source: P_PIAZZA: front beam top sits ~level with the eave

slope_deg.source: P_PIAZZA (beam and ceiling read nearly horizontal)

roof.front_beam: hewn log beam ~8 x 10 in, 22 ft + 1 ft overhangs
roof.covering: boards + sawn shingles; edge visible with shingle butts in P_PIAZZA

east_veranda.steps: none visible; deck 1 ft above grade

south_piazza.evidence: TAY59 p.48 '8 or 9 feet wide and about 14 feet long ... covered by an overhanging shingled roof which sloped down away from the house and was supported by posts at each corner'; MAP57 outline converts to X 8.6-28.7, depth 7.4-7.8 ft; P_HOUSE shows the piazza's east open end running back to the SE corner and the west window just outside its west post; EDITH sketch draws it near the hall door.

X_start.source: MAP57 8.6; P_HOUSE (west window S-W1 lies outside, west of the piazza)

length.note: CONFLICT: Taylor's text 'about 14 feet' and BP (13.4 ft centred) vs Taylor's own excavation map (~20 ft). The map's veranda dimensions match his text exactly, so the map is trusted here; P_HOUSE supports an east end near the SE corner.

back_stoop_west.evidence: TAY59 p.48: 'Roosevelt shows the back door stoop as 6 feet wide by 10 feet long; actually it seems to have been only about [4?] feet by 8 feet ... nothing to indicate whether or not the stoop was roofed over. I rather think not.' Wood from the kitchen door stoop found (p.34). TAY59 fig.20 proportions 0.47 -> ~3.8 x 8 ft.

back_stoop_west.roof: none (recommended); alternative per T.R.'s plan: 6x10 ft with lean-to roof

cellar_hatch_west.evidence: TAY59 p.40, 48: outside entry framed with timbers 3 in x 5.5-6 in x >6 ft, 'set against the wall', ~6 ft by 4 ft, door lay just above ground level and lifted up; eight steps down (six survived), steps reach ~3 ft into the cellar; MAP57 places the frame at Y ~8.8-14.8 projecting ~4.9 ft west of the wall.
cellar_hatch_west.lid: board bulkhead door, hinged on the wall side, lying ~6-10 in above grade, nearly flat (slight fall away from wall)
cellar_hatch_west.steps: 8 plank steps descending EAST under the sill into the west cellar room; rise ~9.5 in, run ~9 in (derived: ~6.3 ft drop)

chimney.evidence: TAY59 pp.35-38, 50: only ONE chimney; brick and mortar rubble (bricks 8 x 3.75 x 2.25 in) over the cellar/passage; a 3-ft section of soot-blackened flue with a metal stove-pipe collar lay across the darkroom passage, base resting on the ground with red-painted lowest courses; it 'had tipped towards the west as it fell, hence must have stood a little nearer the center of the house'; 'almost entirely below the kitchen area'; location 'agrees with that shown in Roosevelt's view across the front veranda'. P_PIAZZA (THRB03304-00217) shows the chimney cap rising above the main roof behind the veranda roof, at top-centre (x~1050/2000, y~150).

plan_position.note: against the kitchen side of the hall's west partition (hall X 14-18)
plan_position.source: TAY59 + MAP57 passage line X~11.7-11.9, shifted E per fall direction

stack_above_roof.section: 1'4" x 2'0" (one 8 x 12 in flue, 4 in brick walls) - estimate

top_z.source: P_PIAZZA: cap clearly visible above roof from ground level ~22 ft away; set 2.5 ft above ridge

stack_above_roof.cap: corbelled brick cap (1-2 projecting courses), light-coloured in P_PIAZZA (possibly lime-washed or mortar-capped)

chimney.brick: soft red common brick 8 x 3 3/4 x 2 1/4 in (TAY59), lime mortar
chimney.base: brick stack from ground (inside the cellar/passage) up through the kitchen; stove-pipe thimble low in kitchen

fireplace.evidence: T.R. (Hunting Trips 1885 p.16): evenings 'round the hearthstone, while the pine logs roar and crackle ... the rifles stand in the corners of the room or rest across the elk antlers which jut out from over the fireplace'; Fred Sewall: Wilmot Dow built the fireplace (MAT60); TAY59 p.50: with only one chimney, 'about the only place the fireplace could have been was also in the kitchen'.
fireplace.recommendation: single brick fireplace on the kitchen's east wall (backing on the hall), opening facing WEST into the kitchen, with the cook-stove piped into the same stack via a thimble; flat sandstone hearthstone in front; plank mantel shelf with an elk rack above.
fireplace.opening: 2'6" W x 2'4" H x 1'4" deep (estimate, Rumford-less ranch fireplace)
fireplace.hearth: sandstone slab ~4'0" x 2'0" (TAY59: a stone 'perhaps the fireplace hearth' was taken to the State Capitol grounds)
fireplace.alternative: BP draws the fireplace in a 'Living Room' on the east side of the hall (X 18-25, Y 18-24). Rejected: no east-side chimney rubble was excavated.

cellar.excavation_outline: rounded pit, walls rounded with no sharp corners, ~12 x 12 ft

west_room.other: flat sandstone with 21 in circular barrel stain south of bottom step

darkroom.partition: horizontal boards on 4 cedar posts (6, 3.5, 3.5, 3.75 in dia, N to S) with battens over joints (light-proofing)

floor_depth_below_grade.source: TAY59 '7 feet 9 inches below ground surface'

darkroom.ceiling: own board ceiling resting on E cellar wall and the partition
darkroom.workbench: boards across the S end; zinc sheet on bench
darkroom.use: T.R.'s photographic darkroom (Mrs. George Harmon, Sewall's daughter, via MAT60)

passage_and_ladder.ladder: 2 cedar poles 24 in apart (3 and 3.5 in dia), nailed rungs
passage_and_ladder.trapdoor: ~2'6" x 2'6" in kitchen floor near NE corner of kitchen (TAY59: 'probably through a trapdoor in the kitchen floor')

interior_plan.status: Recommended layout = Edith Roosevelt's 1890 room sequence (the only complete first-hand plan of the house as built), dimensioned to the excavated cellar/passage/chimney and Taylor's 16 ft kitchen; T.R.'s 1884 sketch (10 rooms) is the original two-family scheme. Interior is the least certain part of the model.

length.source: MAT60: hall 'running from the south door about three-fourths of the [length of the] house'

NW room ('Common room'? - Edith's label partly illegible)

rooms.evidence: EDITH ('Mr Ferguson & Cog Lodge', piazza in front); TRSK 'Sitting Room'

interior_plan.partitions: board partitions of vertical matched pine boards ~1 in thick on 2x4 plates (lumber list: partition boards 18 ft 4,300 bf and 10 ft 600 bf); door openings 2'8" x 6'6" off the hall

Mattison: partitions probably moved 1885-1890 when the house went from two families to one.

Scoria (clinker) path and yard surfacing between house, well, shed and privy (TAY59 p.8); scoria path NW from veranda ~35 ft.

conflicts_resolved.issue: Flat roof (Sewall 1884 letter, 1919 book) vs photos
conflicts_resolved.why: Three independent T.R. photographs, T.R.'s own sketch elevation and the blueprint all show/measure ~30 deg.

conflicts_resolved.issue: Wall height 7 ft (Sewall 1919) vs 9 ft (Sewall 1884 letter) vs 7.5 ft (T.R. sketch) vs 9.2 ft (BP)
conflicts_resolved.decision: Exterior grade-to-plate 9'4" (8 courses x 13.25 in from Z 0'6"); interior clear ~7'6"
conflicts_resolved.why: Photo course count + scale gives ~9 ft at eave outside; 7-7.5 ft is the interior floor-to-ceiling.

conflicts_resolved.issue: Veranda depth 6 ft (Taylor text, excavation map) vs ~9.7 ft (BP) vs 10 ft (T.R. plan) vs ~9-11 ft (weak camera solve)
conflicts_resolved.why: Only the excavation measured the as-built porch; T.R.'s plan and BP are design/conjecture. Validate with camera match #1.

conflicts_resolved.issue: Veranda length 40 ft (T.R. plan), full length (Gifford engraving) vs 22 ft
conflicts_resolved.why: Taylor: 'Neither the archeological evidence nor the photographs support the 40-foot figure'; P_PIAZZA shows W1 outside the veranda; Edith's sketch agrees.

conflicts_resolved.issue: South piazza ~14 ft (Taylor text, BP 13.4) vs ~20 ft (Taylor's excavation map)
conflicts_resolved.why: Map is the measured record and reproduces his veranda text exactly; P_HOUSE shows the piazza's east end reaching the SE corner.

conflicts_resolved.issue: BP porch layout (veranda 20.7 x 9.7 centred; S porch 13.4 x 9.4 centred)
conflicts_resolved.decision: Use BP for window/door spacing only
conflicts_resolved.why: BP agrees with photos on window rhythm but its porches disagree with the excavation.

conflicts_resolved.decision: Model the 8-room 1886-1890 layout; keep T.R.'s 10-room partition set as an alternative layer
conflicts_resolved.why: Mattison: partitions likely moved when the house changed from two families to one; Edith's plan is the only as-built record.

conflicts_resolved.issue: Fireplace location (T.R. sitting-room hearth vs single kitchen chimney)
conflicts_resolved.decision: Kitchen fireplace + stove on one stack at X~13, Y~23
conflicts_resolved.why: Only one chimney excavated, under the kitchen (Taylor).

conflicts_resolved.decision: Yes - one brick stack with light cap visible above the roof in P_PIAZZA; hidden by foliage in P_HOUSE and P_RIVER
conflicts_resolved.why: Direct observation in THRB03304-00217 at full resolution; Taylor/Mattison 1960 note the chimney agrees with the 'view across the front veranda'.

open_uncertainties: Veranda depth (6.25 ft recommended; 6-10 ft plausible).
South piazza length (20 ft recommended; 14 ft per Taylor's text).
West and north window positions and the back stoop (no photographs).
Corner-notch type (projection certain, notch geometry not resolvable).
The dark band at Z ~1.3-2.0 ft on the east wall.
Interior partitions (only Edith's sketch and Taylor's conjectural plan).
Exact chimney plan position (+/-3 ft) and height.
